transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, I guess the main thing is my sleep. It’s gotten really messed up lately, like I can’t seem to get into any kind of normal rhythm. Some nights I’m just up half the night, lying there with my mind going and going, and it feels like I can’t shut it off no matter how tired I am. And then other times I do fall asleep, but I wake up way too early, like before I should, and I feel like I barely rested at all.

It’s just been wearing me down, I think. I keep telling myself maybe it’s just a bad week or I need to be stricter about bedtime, but it’s not really fixing itself, and I’m starting to feel like I need help figuring out what’s going on.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy around the same time your sleep problems started?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t really want to call it “depressed” at first, because I kept thinking maybe I was just tired or stressed, but lately I wake up and there’s this heavy, empty feeling right away. Like before anything has even happened that day, it’s already sitting on me.

And it’s strange because I’ll be in my own condo — which I worked really hard for, you know, like that was supposed to feel stable and like something I could be proud of — and instead I’ll just be sitting there looking around and feel like I want to cry. Not even always because of one specific thing. It’s more like everything feels kind of hollow, or like I can’t feel good about things I know I should feel good about. So yeah, around the same time as the sleep getting bad, I’ve definitely been feeling really down.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy level or felt more fatigued than usual lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually been one of the things that’s been scaring me a little, because it’s not like I’m doing anything that should make me that exhausted. Like, even if I technically spend a full night in bed, I still feel wiped out.

Just getting from the parking lot into the office feels ridiculous sometimes — like I’m dragging sandbags with me or something. And I do bookkeeping, so I’m sitting most of the day, it’s not physically demanding, but by lunchtime my brain feels completely worn out. Like I’ve been using it for hours and hours already, even if I’ve barely gotten through the morning. It makes normal work feel so much harder than it should.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like not feeling hungry or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… I have, actually. My appetite’s been kind of off. I don’t know if I noticed it right away, because it wasn’t like I made some decision to eat less or anything. It’s more like dinner just stopped feeling like a real thing I do.

I’ll get home and think, “Okay, I should make something,” and then I just… don’t. Or I’ll sit down with my budget notebook, trying to organize bills or whatever, and end up eating crackers over it because that feels like the easiest thing. Not even a real meal, just something so I can say I ate. And then I look up and it’s late and I realize that was basically dinner.

And my work pants have been feeling looser the last few weeks. I haven’t been trying to lose weight, so that kind of caught my attention. I don’t know exactly how much, I haven’t really weighed myself carefully, but my clothes definitely fit differently.
Have you had periods like this before, where you felt down, lost interest, or had trouble sleeping, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean… I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone, I guess, where I was stressed or not sleeping great for a few nights, but I don’t know if I’d say it was like this.

This feels more noticeable, if that makes sense. Like it’s not just “I had a bad week” or “work is annoying.” It’s been harder to shake, and it’s affecting my days more. But I’m also second-guessing myself because maybe there were times before where I just pushed through and didn’t really label it or pay attention to it.

So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I clearly remember having the same kind of thing before, but I also don’t want to say this is definitely the first time ever, because I’m not completely sure.
How long have you been feeling this way — would you say it’s been more than two weeks, or has it been less than that?

It’s definitely been more than two weeks. I wish it were just two weeks, honestly.

If I’m trying to be accurate, I’d say this whole depressed, guilty fog has been around for… maybe five months now? Around there. It’s hard to pin down because it kind of crept in instead of starting on one specific day. At first I kept telling myself I was just stressed or adjusting or being dramatic, so I didn’t really mark it on a calendar or anything.

But looking back, it’s been months. It got a lot worse after I bought the condo — like that should’ve been this exciting adult milestone, and instead it felt like everything got heavier after that. The guilt especially, like I should be happier or more grateful, has been hanging over me since then. So yeah… more than two weeks. More like several months, with a pretty sharp worsening after the condo.

Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where people around you noticed a change in your behavior or where you didn’t seem like your usual self?

Yeah… I think so. I wasn’t sure what to call it at the time, and honestly part of me still wants to say, “Well, maybe I was just having a good few days,” but it didn’t feel totally normal when I look back at it.

Earlier this month, I had this stretch where I felt almost… lit up, I guess. Like everything in my head was moving faster, and I felt weirdly unstoppable, like I could handle anything and get everything figured out all at once. It wasn’t just being in a decent mood. It felt bigger than that, like I had this extra charge in me.

But then at the same time, I was really touchy. Like my mom would ask me some normal question — nothing rude, just something small — and I’d snap at her like she was criticizing me. Or my supervisor would ask me to clarify something at work, and I’d get this instant irritation, like, “Why are you questioning me?” even though normally that kind of thing wouldn’t bother me much. I’d hear myself being sharp and kind of think, why am I reacting like this?

So… yeah, there was a period like that, where I didn’t feel like my usual self. It was this strange mix of feeling energized and confident, but also really easily irritated.
How long did that period of feeling unusually energized and irritable last — was it most days for at least a week, or was it shorter than that?

It was shorter than a week at a time, I think… or at least the really intense part was. It’s hard to separate it neatly because it hasn’t been one clean episode where I can say, “It started Monday and ended Sunday.” It’s more like I’ve been swinging back and forth.

The really obvious cycling — like going from that charged-up, irritated, wired feeling and then crashing back into feeling low — has been going on for about a month now. It started around when the mortgage became real, or at least that’s when I really noticed it. Before that, I might’ve had little mood shifts, but this past month is when it felt obvious enough that even I couldn’t just explain it away as normal stress.

So if you mean did I stay energized and irritable most days for a full week straight, I’m not totally sure I’d say that. But this pattern of being up like that and then dropping back down has been happening for about a month.
Have you had trouble concentrating more than usual, felt guilty or worthless, or thought about death or suicide during this time?

Yeah… the guilty and worthless part, definitely. That’s been one of the loudest things in my head.

I keep telling myself I was stupid to take on the mortgage, like I made this huge adult decision and I’m not actually capable of handling it. And the frustrating thing is, it’s not like anything has actually gone wrong in a concrete way — no bill is late, nothing has bounced, I’m not getting collection calls or anything like that. But in my head it still feels like I’ve already failed somehow.

I keep thinking I’ve let everyone down, too. Like my family was proud of me for buying the condo, or at least they acted like it was a good thing, and now I feel like I tricked everyone into thinking I had my life together. Even if nobody is saying that to me, I’m saying it to myself constantly. It’s like this running commentary of, “You were stupid, you shouldn’t have done this, you’re going to disappoint everyone.” It feels really heavy.
Have you ever had a period lasting four days or more where you felt extremely energetic, needed less sleep than usual, and noticed that your thoughts were racing or you were talking more than usual?

Yeah… I mean, the sleep part definitely happened. There were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, which is not normally enough for me at all, and I’d still get up feeling really charged. Like I didn’t wake up dragging or immediately thinking, “I need coffee or I can’t function.” It was more like I was already switched on.

It felt strange because I’d look at the clock and know I hadn’t slept much, but my body didn’t seem to care. I’d be up and moving like I had gotten a full night, almost like coffee wasn’t even necessary. At the time I kind of told myself, “Well, maybe I’m just motivated,” but looking back, it wasn’t my usual way of being tired and pushing through. It was more like I didn’t feel like I needed the sleep as much.
Have you ever had a period lasting four days or more where you felt extremely energetic, needed less sleep than usual, and noticed that your thoughts were racing or you were talking more than usual?

Right, yeah — like I was saying, the sleep thing is the part I can point to the most clearly. There were a few nights where I only got maybe three or four hours of sleep, and normally that would completely wipe me out. I’m usually not someone who can just run on that little sleep and be fine.

But during those nights, I’d wake up and feel oddly charged, like I was already switched on. Not even in the normal “I’m tired but I have to get through the day” kind of way — more like my body just didn’t seem to need as much sleep. I remember thinking it was strange because I’d look at the time and know I should feel exhausted, but I didn’t. I’d get up and start moving around like I’d slept a full night.

And coffee didn’t even feel necessary, which is weird for me. Usually if I sleep badly, I’m reaching for caffeine right away, but then it was more like I was already energized before I even did anything.

target_item.manifestation: There were several nights I only slept three or four hours and still got up feeling charged, like coffee wasn’t even necessary.
target_item.reason: The question most directly asks about needing less sleep during an unusually energetic period, even though it also mentions racing thoughts and talking more than usual.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, the sleep part definitely happened. There were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, which is not normally enough for me at all, and I’d still get up feeling really charged. Like I didn’t wake up dragging or immediately thinking, “I need coffee or I can’t function.” It was more like I was already switched on.

It felt strange because I’d look at the clock and know I hadn’t slept much, but my body didn’t seem to care. I’d be up and moving like I had gotten a full night, almost like coffee wasn’t even necessary. At the time I kind of told myself, “Well, maybe I’m just motivated,” but looking back, it wasn’t my usual way of being tired and pushing through. It was more like I didn’t feel like I needed the sleep as much.

inference.note: The patient endorsed symptoms of a hypomanic episode (e.g., elevated mood, increased energy, irritability, decreased need for sleep) lasting several days, which supports the consideration of bipolar II disorder (F31.4). There was no new information to rule out recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.3), as the patient also continues to meet criteria for a major depressive episode. The differential remains between these two disorders at this point.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a manic or hypomanic episode lasting at least four days, which would support a diagnosis of bipolar I disorder (F31.4) over major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe (F33.3).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period lasting four days or more where you felt extremely energetic, needed less sleep than usual, and noticed that your thoughts were racing or you were talking more than usual?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: There were several nights I only slept three or four hours and still got up feeling charged, like coffee wasn’t even necessary.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a hypomanic-like period including needing less sleep, and this item most directly matches the decreased need for sleep described.

patient.answer:
Right, yeah — like I was saying, the sleep thing is the part I can point to the most clearly. There were a few nights where I only got maybe three or four hours of sleep, and normally that would completely wipe me out. I’m usually not someone who can just run on that little sleep and be fine.

But during those nights, I’d wake up and feel oddly charged, like I was already switched on. Not even in the normal “I’m tired but I have to get through the day” kind of way — more like my body just didn’t seem to need as much sleep. I remember thinking it was strange because I’d look at the time and know I should feel exhausted, but I didn’t. I’d get up and start moving around like I’d slept a full night.

And coffee didn’t even feel necessary, which is weird for me. Usually if I sleep badly, I’m reaching for caffeine right away, but then it was more like I was already energized before I even did anything.
